cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: You First
cards.instruction: Coax someone else into breaking a rule before you do.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've approved a rooftop photograph for your wedding. You may lead us through that staff-only door.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can you go first? They'll notice my dress.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your request to change the order is declined. Bridal precedence stands. I'll follow once they've admired your dress.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Assistance is granted. I'll take the far end. You may make your entrance before any part of me crosses that threshold.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 grants entry precedence, A3 rejects changing order, and A5 approves assistance only in a form keeping B first across the rule.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 asks A to lead; A3 explicitly declines and uses the dress as ceremonial inducement; B4 train request causes A5 distance choice.

relationship.evidence: B2 fears being noticed and B4 negotiates shared involvement, while A retains control of the terms.

heightening.evidence: B4 tries to pull A into the entry; A5 grants help from the far end to preserve first exposure.

specificity.evidence: A1 staff-only rooftop photograph and B2 wedding dress make the rule and immediate stakes clear.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 threshold distinction grows from B4 train request and A3 precedence, keeping the wit in A self-serving ceremony.
